Principal Findings: 1) TSPOT: Cumulative incidence of active TB higher in IGRA+ compared to IGRA- individuals, but difference not statistically significant (10% vs. 0%, risk difference 10%, 95% CI -3% to +23%). 2) QGT-GIT: Cumulative incidence of active TB higher in IGRA+ compared to IGRA- individuals, but difference not statistically significant (8% vs. 0%, risk difference 8%, 95% CI -0.7% to 17%).
What do these findings mean?: IGRA+ individuals may have a higher risk of progression to active TB than IGRA- individuals, but the risk of progression is low in both groups.

Outcome: Sensitivity for active TB (a surrogate reference standard for LTBI)
Principal Findings: 1) TSPOT: Pooled sensitivity 72% (95% CI 62-81%); TSPOT more sensitive than TST in 1 study, less sensitive in 1 study, and as sensitive in 1 study. 2) QFT-GIT: Pooled sensitivity was 61% (95% CI 47-75%). Compared to TST, QFT-GIT more sensitive in 1 study and less sensitive in 1 study.
What do these findings mean?: In low- and middle-income countries, IGRAs have suboptimal sensitivity for active TB and do not consistently have higher sensitivity than TST.

Principal Findings: 1) TSPOT: Pooled concordance 77% (95% CI 67-88%). 2) QFT-GIT: 1 study; concordance 91%.
What do these findings mean?: In low- and middle-income countries, IGRAs have moderate concordance with TST.
